fixed.text: Vault-like particles from prokaryotic and phage MVP homologs occur after expression in Escherichia coli. Cell-free screening is described as 44 expressed proteins and as 44 constructs encoding 43 distinct homologs. Further screening has 25 heterologously expressed proteins evaluated, seven homologs with vault-like particles in negative-stain images, four confirmed by cryo-EM, and a broader count of eight particle-forming homologs. These are different screening stages; their complete reconciliation remains open. Large particles and aggregates both occur in excluded-volume chromatography fractions. The empty-vector preparation has sparse grids with no barrels or ring/arc fragments. Bc1 appears ring-like under negative stain and vault-like under cryo-EM. Negative-stain appearance alone establishes no absolute absence of vault formation. Formation in the organisms of origin remains unobserved in this work.

fixed.section: 3.7 Structural-protein surface — a matrix as a living set: a self
fixed.text: The L05 vault reconstruction places seven repeats end to end within each chain, neighboring chains side by side along wall seams, and two half-shells meeting at a waist, with 48 chains per half and 96 in the shell. Human vaults have nine repeats and 39 chains per half, 78 in the shell. L05+2 has nine repeats and retains 48 chains per half. The reported dimensions are approximately 54.5 × 47.5 nm for L05, 58.5 × 49.4 nm for L05+2, and 67 × 40 nm for the human comparison. L05’s volume is approximately 25% above the human comparison; L05+2’s is approximately 20% above L05 and 50% above the human comparison. Wall lengths are 28.1 nm for L05 and 35.3 nm for human vaults, a 7.2 nm difference; cap angles approximately 34° and 52°. The added-repeat variant changes wall curvature by approximately 16° and relative waist orientation by approximately 3° while retaining reported chain count and wall/cap symmetry. These are structural comparisons of preparations, no single shell’s enlargement or adaptation observed.

fixed.section: 3.7 Structural-protein surface — a matrix as a living set: a self
fixed.text: L05 cryo-EM processing reports 3,041 frozen-sample acquisition movies, 34,337 initially selected particles, 28,358 after two-dimensional classification, 19,389 complete particles and 11,945 closed complete particles after three-dimensional classification without imposed symmetry. A preliminary reconstruction without symmetry favors 48 wall ribs; cap classification supports 16-fold and eight-fold descriptions. Final reconstructions include D16, C16 and C8 averaging; D8 operations generate a 96-chain model from six chains. Initial reconstruction has mirror ambiguity, a smoothed predicted shell with 48 copies per half helps later initialization, and alpha-helical features and mirrored alternatives inform the handedness choice. Nominal approximately 3.2 Å resolution is a mean across five local reconstructions; approximately 717–724 of 866 residues per chain are modeled and the linker between repeats 6 and 7 remains unresolved. L05+2 whole-vault reconstruction reaches 8.1 Å before half-vault processing with C48 symmetry; the whole model combines a half and its copy with partner density supporting the relative orientation, and some fitting to noise is acknowledged. Acquiring exposures of frozen particles and constructing these models is distinct from following one particle assembling continuously.

fixed.section: 3.7 Structural-protein surface — a matrix as a living set: a self
fixed.text: Cellular cryo-electron tomography in Dictyostelium reports 999 vaults in 318 tomograms: 14 membrane-associated vaults and 84 enclosing ribosomes, four of those membrane-associated and 80 cytosolic. No isolated half-vaults are detected in that sample, which overrepresents the nuclear periphery. Frozen associations do not order contact, enclosure or passage, and do not establish the native function of L05 particles. A separate cryo-EM study classifies full vaults as 32% symmetric and 68% asymmetric, with 9.6% half-vaults on the grid excluded from that classification. Whether an asymmetric form is a disassembly intermediate remains open. Variability animations, principal-component animations and simulations are distinct from following one physical vault continuously.
